researchQuestion:
Main question: Among first-generation college students in Texas, how do financial strain and faculty support relate to academic burnout?

Subquestions:
1. Does academic self-efficacy explain these relationships?
2. Does the relationship between academic self-efficacy and academic burnout differ by years in the united states?
hypotheses:
H1 (direct): Higher financial strain will be associated with lower academic self-efficacy.

H2 (direct): Higher faculty support will be associated with higher academic self-efficacy.

H3 (direct): Higher academic self-efficacy will be associated with lower academic burnout.

H4 (moderation): The link between academic self-efficacy and academic burnout will differ by years in the united states (under 5 years vs. 5 or more years).

H5 (mediation): Academic self-efficacy will mediate the links from financial strain and faculty support to academic burnout.
